newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's oil, gas exports rise 29 percent in 1996. [CORRECTED 09:12 GMT 19/1]
newsitem.headline: Algeria's oil, gas exports rise 29 percent in 1996. [CORRECTED 09:12 GMT 19/1]

text.p: The value of Algeria's exports of oil and gas rose by 29 percent to $12.5 billion in 1996 from the year before, Energy and Mining Minister Amar Makhloufi told state-run radio on Saturday.
Energy officials said the rise was mainly due to higher international oil prices.

Makhloufi, who was not asked to comment on the reasons for the higher exports, said Algeria earned an average $21.50 (corrects from $22.50) per barrel in 1996 against a budgeted average of $16-17 per barrel.
Algeria's oil and gas exports were worth $9.7 billion in 1995 against $8.5 billion, according to official figures.
The government has forecast $538 million of non-oil and gas exports for 1996 compared with $350 million in the previous year.
Algeria has forecast $16 billion in receipts from oil and gas exports by the year 2000, thanks mostly to increased gas exports.
